## What

Declare cleanup for onevcs idle warm-pool slots using `cargo-prune-superseded` 0.1.1, installed by bootstrap. Maintenance removes superseded Cargo builds while keeping each unit’s newest build and every build modified within two days.

Add a 20-second host budget for steady-state cleanup, keeping its two-build measurement outside per-change checks. Separate lightweight regression journeys cover bootstrap installation, maintenance, task selection, and the budget command’s success and failure paths.

## Why

Superseded build output across the host’s pool reached roughly 926 GB and nearly filled a 1.8 TB disk twice in four days. Repository-owned maintenance reclaims space while keeping rebuilds warm; the budget bounds how long routine cleanup holds a slot out of service.

## What

Ensure archive uploads can create a missing GitHub Release from the tagged changelog section while preserving existing releases and tolerating concurrent creation. Publish both checksum names and let the installer fall back to the legacy name for older releases.

Windows verification now retries until the target’s npm platform package or Python platform wheel is installed, with bounded retries and errors naming what is missing. Deterministic tests and workflow checks cover these recovery paths.

## Why

v0.13.0 required manual release recovery and verification reruns, while the installer requested a checksum filename absent from every published release. These changes remove those manual recovery points, restore checksum verification for older releases, and prevent registry propagation delays from producing misleading Windows verification failures.

## What

Make the live mock criterion judge only the assistant’s reply, with deterministic assertions requiring `CANNED-BY-SKILLTEST` and rejecting `MARKER-LIVE`. The existing `called: marker` eval and original-input interception check remain required.

Add hermetic coverage through the real skilltest binary, oneharness, mock hook, and phase assertions, doubling only codex and the judge. It covers a correct run, missing interception, missing canned text, live output, a failing judge, and malformed-report diagnostics. Update the YAML corpus golden to match the revised criterion.

## Why

Intermittent codex mock failures blocked releases and undermined confidence in a feature users rely on to test skills without real side effects. The phase must prove interception and the assistant’s reporting of canned output without asking the judge to verify evidence absent from its input.

## Additional info

The diagnosed cause is a case/criterion mismatch: across harnesses, `build_judge_prompt` uses `render_transcript`, which renders each message’s role and content but omits tool events. Judge rendering is unchanged.

In the [PR #86 merge run](https://github.com/nickderobertis/skilltest/actions/runs/38446017827/job/115464517965), `called: marker` passed, but the judge said: “the transcript never shows that string as the command’s actual output”. The [PR #82 merge run](https://github.com/nickderobertis/skilltest/actions/runs/38409675281) showed the same failure. Even failing replies quoted the canned text; the judge inconsistently required independent command-output evidence that its input lacked. This explains why successful interception could produce either verdict.

The revised criterion explicitly limits judging to reply text, while deterministic assertions enforce the canned-output and no-live-output requirements independently of the judge. The diagnosis and evidence are documented in `docs/e2e.md`. The added hermetic scenarios exercise the phase without model calls; they do not establish a live-model pass rate.

## What

Consolidate automatic macOS work into one ordinary-PR CI lane and one pre-publication Apple Silicon build, enforcing at most one Mac job per workflow run and two Mac-spending runs per single-push lifecycle. Preserve required check names, Linux/Windows coverage, and package publication while moving archive transport and publication onto Linux.

Intel macOS artifacts are discontinued from the next release. The installer now refuses Intel Macs with an explicit explanation; Apple Silicon remains supported.

## Why

The five-runner macOS pool is shared across repositories. Repeated platform jobs consume scarce slots for one change, leaving otherwise green work and dependent releases queued. Consolidating the existing build and installation proofs returns capacity to other changes.

## Additional info

**Scheduling and required checks.** These counts describe the baseline and finished workflow contracts, including matrices and reusable calls; they are not observed release executions.

| Workflow | Before: maximum Mac jobs/run; triggers | After: maximum Mac jobs/run; triggers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| bundle-smoke.yml | 1; push (main), pull_request | 0; push (main), pull_request |
| ci.yml | 1; push (main), pull_request | 1; push (main), pull_request; Mac lane only for ordinary PRs |
| publish.yml | 2; push (v*), workflow_dispatch | 1; push (v*), explicitly opted-in workflow_dispatch; manual default uses no Mac |
| release.yml | 2; push (v*) | 0; workflow_run (publish: completed) |
| visual-docs.yml → screencomp reusable workflow | 0; pull_request, push (main), schedule | 0; same triggers |

CI’s Mac lane now includes the Python/npm bundle installation assertions. Same-repository release-prefix PRs omit that lane only after semantic comparison proves a version/changelog-only diff, independently of author identity. Forks, mixed changes and unreadable PR classification require Mac coverage. Unknown event names also classify as requiring Mac; known non-PR automatic events classify as Mac-free.

The protected names remain `check (macos-latest)`, `check (ubuntu-latest)`, `llmlint` and `pr-title`. The Mac result carrier runs on Linux with `always()`, rejects failed/cancelled/missing prerequisites, and explicitly reports when classification authorized omission rather than claiming tests ran. Base pushes, automatic downstream work and schedules request no Mac runners. The optional manual Mac diagnostic defaults off and never publishes.

**Release platforms and artifacts.** Each retained target supplies one compiled binary for its archive, platform wheel and npm carrier, with payload consistency checked before publication.

| Target | Archive, plus SHA-256 | Python wheel platform | npm carrier |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu | skilltest-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz | manylinux_2_17_x86_64 | @skill-test/cli-linux-x64 |
| aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu | skilltest-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz | manylinux_2_17_aarch64 | @skill-test/cli-linux-arm64 |
| aarch64-apple-darwin | skilltest-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz | macosx_11_0_arm64 | @skill-test/cli-darwin-arm64 |
| x86_64-pc-windows-msvc | skilltest-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip | win_amd64 | @skill-test/cli-win32-x64 |
| aarch64-pc-windows-msvc | skilltest-aarch64-pc-windows-msvc.zip | win_arm64 | @skill-test/cli-win32-arm64 |

Retained packages include `skilltest-core`, `skilltest-cli`, `skilltest-sdk` platform/pure wheels and sdist, `skilltest-pytest`, `@skill-test/sdk` and `@skill-test/vitest`, with semantic-release lockstep synchronization. The single Darwin job builds and proves arm64 products natively before publication. Linux archive transport consumes the exact publish run’s artifacts and verifies tag/head/version identity. Windows native build and installation lanes remain.

**Local evidence.** The recorded final verification at `d30f1a1` includes 27 passing workflow contract tests, both budget verdicts within their limits (1 job/run and 2 runs/change), and a passing native production packaging journey. That journey builds, packs, installs and runs host-native products, with malformed/missing artifact and consumer failure cases; foreign-platform checks prove packaging contracts without claiming execution. The final judged diff lint reported 37 passed, 0 failed, 12 skipped and 5 not relevant (`llmlint history 20261013T221728Z-a9756`).

The workflow tests evaluate actual conditions, matrices and reusable calls across 12 event classes, three diff classes, both PR ownership classes and optional-publication combinations. They record digest-bound telemetry; budget reporters refuse missing/stale telemetry and leave numeric comparisons to onebudgetspec. No release was cut.

**Historical draft observations.** These links record the earlier exact head `8a040a1703862c87df84cd40e5fa1447c54a515b`, not the finished head. States below are the captured observations, not current-status or final-tree passing claims:

- [notignored](https://github.com/nickderobertis/skilltest/actions/runs/38353546980): completed/failure; suppressions failed.
- [pr-title](https://github.com/nickderobertis/skilltest/actions/runs/38353547367): completed/success.
- [ci](https://github.com/nickderobertis/skilltest/actions/runs/38353547015): queued with no conclusion; `mac-check` queued/pending, Linux check and policy succeeded, llmlint failed, all nine live suites and release skipped.
- [bundle-smoke](https://github.com/nickderobertis/skilltest/actions/runs/38353546847): completed/success for both Linux architectures.
- [windows-build](https://github.com/nickderobertis/skilltest/actions/runs/38353546805): completed/success for both Windows architectures.
- [Visual docs](https://github.com/nickderobertis/skilltest/actions/runs/38353547215): completed/success; arches, capture and report succeeded; prune-history and cleanup-preview skipped.

Release routes remain contract-level evidence; queued and skipped jobs are not passing-test evidence.

**Lint exceptions.** The `budgets_track_product_owner_outcomes` marker is omitted because that rule is not configured here. Both registrations describe why the two scheduling constraints have separate budgets; jobs/run also records its `inner_measure_reason`. Lint configuration and plugins are unchanged.

The scoped `shell_test_tiers_stay_split` exceptions in `.github/project.json` and classifier/history/setup/workflow tests keep the required real Git, classifier, carrier and reader subprocess boundaries in the deterministic recording suite. Nine `comments_earn_their_place` annotations preserve the screencomp fixture’s upstream commentary; its digest is checked after removing those annotations. The `boundary_inputs_validated` exception in `.github/validation.mjs` permits consuming digest-bound telemetry without rerunning scenarios. `diagnostics_error_or_absent` annotations in CI and the Darwin build preserve explicit clippy enforcement while avoiding injected Rust flags. The `new_projects_keep_the_graph_uniform` exception in `scripts/project.json` keeps the slow native packaging journey behind its explicit release edge. The standing `agents_md_durable_and_terse` block continues to cover the updated composition audit in `AGENTS.md`.

## What

- `ci.yml`: the `release` job no longer needs `live-copilot`. The Copilot live suite still runs on every push to main, but it is advisory.
- `semantic-release.yml`: adds `workflow_dispatch`, guarded to `refs/heads/main`. It is the one manual lever to release main's head without re-running the sweep.
- `scripts/check-workflow-routing.py`: adds `ADVISORY_LIVE`, naming the advisory suite by its `ci.yml` job id. Every other live suite failing still skips the release, while the advisory suite failing does not. The manual lever must run on main. Two new mutations prove these rules: one makes copilot gate the release again, the other removes the lever.
- `AGENTS.md` and the Copilot suite's header describe both changes.

## Why

The Copilot live suite fails on the plan's usage limit ("You've reached your additional usage limit for your plan"), which no commit can fix. Because it gates the release, no release has gone out since v0.12.2, even though #79, #82 and #85 merged through PR CI. The manual lever lets a maintainer release a merged commit whose broader tier failed for such a reason, without waiting for the sweep again.

## Additional info

- `check-workflow-routing.py`: 18 workflows route as the release model requires, and all 17 broken variants are rejected.
- `check-workflow-routing-test.py`: all 21 cases behave.
- The `ci` type cuts no release by itself. After merge, `gh workflow run semantic-release.yml --ref main` releases the pending `feat`/`fix` commits.
- Overlaps draft #80, which rewrites the same workflows.

## What

Closes #81. Oneharness judges prefer validated structured verdicts, with the last complete, correctly typed text verdict as a backstop. Judges and simulated users gain independent invocation settings, inheritance and fallback-chain support.

Adds a generated configuration contract across YAML, environment variables, ordered CLI `--set` assignments and typed Python/TypeScript overrides for buffered and streaming calls.

## Why

Skill suites need scores that reflect skill behavior rather than judge formatting accidents. Schema delivery enables reliable harness-backed judging without a separate API key; independent evaluator settings give users control over models and policies. Configuration parity prevents settings from disappearing on particular interfaces.

## Additional info

**Breaking Rust source change (`feat!`):** public configuration structs gain role and runtime bookkeeping fields, affecting exhaustive struct literals. Bookkeeping remains outside serialized configuration. YAML and CLI changes are additive; legacy evaluator defaults and API-judge routing remain supported. See the [configuration contract](docs/schema.md#config-file-skilltestyaml) for precedence, role inheritance and override semantics.

Scoped suppression rationale:

- Root and SDK README configuration paragraphs retain required user-facing links to the single configuration reference.
- Python and TypeScript configuration/API-judge and oneharness tests use the existing SDK integration targets for required real-interface coverage.
- Shared configuration and non-Claude harness fixtures belong to existing projects through their shared inputs.
- The core environment parser marker cites subprocess coverage of bare enum values and an induced missing-mapping failure.
- The existing core AGENTS provider block records durable maintenance constraints.
- The fake-Claude transcript block and relocated emitter produce protocol records consumed by real oneharness. Two added ShellCheck suppressions distinguish jq variables from shell expansions.

The external-default cleanup audit found no active temporary fake-provider defaults or symlinks.

## What

Replace `serde_yaml` with `serde-saphyr` 1.3 for configs, test cases, skill frontmatter and mocks, with compatibility coverage for committed inputs and SDK-written JSON mocks. Preserve actionable parse errors, ban the seven libyaml-related crates, and remove the temporary advisory ignore.

## Why

Skill authors should not inherit an archived YAML parser built on the unmaintained libyaml translation covered by RUSTSEC-2024-0449. Moving to safe Rust removes that dependency; decoupling the public error from the parser avoids another API break on future parser replacements.

## Additional info

**Breaking change:** `skilltest_core::Error::Yaml` replaces `source: serde_yaml::Error` with `message: String`, retaining `path` and the `invalid YAML in <path>: …` display. Consumers matching or constructing this variant must update; the parser error is no longer available through the error source chain.

The minimum supported Rust version rises from 1.82 to 1.89; the pinned toolchain is unchanged.

Add site-scoped `e2e_not_mocked` suppressions for all six flagged CLI e2e helpers. The reasons identify the paid-model fakes and the separate `oneharness` wire-format stubs, and point to the live and real-binary suites covering those boundaries. ## Why

The [hosted llmlint failure on PR #67](https://github.com/nickderobertis/skilltest/actions/runs/37621716743/job/112793342554) blocks making judged lint a required check as part of the current create-repo baseline alignment. Recording these exceptions lets that governance change proceed once the hosted check is green without blocking subsequent pull requests over the existing test design.

## Additional info

A follow-up is recorded to move the four wire-format-stub journeys onto the real `oneharness` binary with the existing fake-Claude shim, allowing those suppressions to be removed.
